unit.title: 3D Shapes
unit.blurb: Naming cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, pyramids and prisms, and counting their faces, edges and vertices.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Identify, describe and sort 3D shapes, including prisms and pyramids, and find them in everyday objects.

O2.t: Count the faces, edges and vertices of 3D shapes.

p: **3D shapes** are solid. You can hold them. They have length, width and height.
The **cylinder** shown looks like a tin of beans.
Shapes with a **curved surface** can roll: sphere, cylinder and cone.
Shapes with only **flat faces** cannot roll: cube, cuboid, pyramid. They slide.

lesson.t: How do I name a 3D shape?
p: Step 1: Look at the faces – flat or curved?
Step 2: Look at the shape of the faces – squares, rectangles, triangles, circles?
Step 3: Match it to the table.

lesson.q: A box has 6 rectangle faces. Name it.
Which rolls: a cone or a pyramid?
steps: A cone has a curved surface

Look for 3D shapes at home: tins, boxes and balls.

lesson.t: What are faces, edges and vertices?
p: A **face** is a flat side. An **edge** is where two faces meet. A **vertex** is a corner (more than one: **vertices**).
Look at the cuboid shown. Its faces are all rectangles.

lesson.t: How many does each shape have?

p: Step 1: Count the top and the bottom.
Step 2: Count the faces round the sides.

lesson.q: How many triangle faces does a square-based pyramid have?
How many vertices does a cuboid have?

p: A picture hides the back. Imagine the whole shape.
Put a sticker on each face as you count. Then you will not count one twice.
